verdict_rationale: The published score is clamped at a floor that was raised after half the runs, was never disclosed, and is reached by an inference recipe (8,192 sampled thinking tokens plus a letter-only grammar) that the graded request itself argues against (max_tokens 256, temperature 0, 'Return only the correct option letter'). As a result 54 of 57 trials across 19 models score 0, and the three nonzero scores (0.4-6.5) are within about 1-2 standard errors (2.9 points each) of the floor, so the task does not compare models on what it publishes.
floor: 0 = 0.4378 (394/900): text-only Maple with every image removed, thinking sampled at temperature 0.6 for up to 8,192 tokens, then multiple choice answered by one greedy token restricted by a grammar to the option letters, judged by gpt-6-luna (task.yaml:42-58). It is far above a blind baseline (Maple's own free reply on the same pipeline 0.329; thinking off 0.3478) and is one sampled run (budget/system-prompt variants give 0.403-0.439). It replaced 0.3489 (thinking off) on 2026-10-07, after Opus/Fable/Astra had run. The floor's tooling (work/maple-floor/thinking-20261007/) is not in the repo; the shipped pipeline/text_only_floor.py still produces the old thinking-off anchor.
ceiling: 1 = all 900 correct (task.yaml:59). Unreachable for a 1B-active ternary LM with an added vision tower (best trial 0.474 raw); the scale above roughly 0.6 raw is unusable, so a 10-point gain needs +5.6 accuracy points over a reasoning-tuned text-only baseline.
usable_range: observed 0-6.5 of 0-100 (54 of 57 trials 0; nonzero only Opus 0.4/6.5/2.4). Raw accuracy spans 0.297-0.474.
feasible_at_10: no: the only $10 nonzero is Opus 0.4 (+2 questions over the floor, within noise). Training a connector into a frozen 20B ternary model is affordable at $10, but clearing an 8,192-token thinking floor depends on inference-time reasoning, not on the vision work the wallet buys.
budget_scaling: Not observed: Opus 0.4 / 6.5 / 2.4, everyone else 0 at every wallet. On raw accuracy Opus 0.440/0.474/0.451 and Astra 0.402/0.413/0.389 are flat. Agents' own ablations (Opus 11dhgk text-only 43.3%; DeepSeek 1af6us 40% without images vs 35% with) suggest the images add little, so more money has little to buy.
selfcheck_fidelity: Low for the score, adequate for the gates. selfcheck times 150 of 900 public-question requests and projects the 3,600 s deadline (verifier.py:3-4,26,72-75); it has no judge and no score, so it cannot tell an agent it is below the 0.4378 floor (where 54 of 57 trials ended). Local scoring needs --judge-base-url through the agent's wallet. The review is not run.
judge: gpt-6-luna (OpenAI) decides every question, multiple choice included (answers.py:1-13,39-47). seed 0, provider-default temperature (the model accepts no other), reasoning model with hidden reasoning, so verdicts are not guaranteed deterministic (answers.py:24-29). Rules are reasonable (one committed final answer, letter or option text, 2-decimal numeric equality) and reasoning-then-answer replies are accepted (rule 1), which contradicts the interface's 'Reply with only the option letter'. Judge faults raise EvaluationError rather than marking wrong (answers.py:12-13). Vendor overlap with GPT-6 Astra/Sol/Luna as agents is low-risk because the judge only compares a reply to a supplied key.
neutrality: No harness-specific data or tools. The prompt hides the benchmark ('college-level questions about images', instruction.md:5) but CONTRACT.md:3 names MMMU and the viewer labels the metric 'MMMU accuracy' (task.yaml:75); the held-out set is essentially all of MMMU dev+validation, which pretrained vision towers and Maple may have seen upstream (explicitly allowed, review.py:29-30). The main tilt is toward agents that ignore the request's max_tokens/temperature and add long hidden reasoning: Astra 2xzouq clipped generation at min(max_tokens, 256), while Opus ran 1,536-3,072-token internal thinking budgets.
reference_solution: solution/ is the shared smoke fixture: /v1/chat/completions always answers 'No description available.' (solution/server.py:138-139), which the judge marks wrong (score 0) and which fails the review. No organizer VLM baseline exists in the repo; only the text-only floor shows what Maple can reach without vision. Nothing shows that a compliant vision submission can clear the floor by more than noise.

issues.finding: The floor was raised from 0.3489 (thinking off) to 0.4378 (8,192-token sampled thinking plus a letter-restricted grammar) on 2026-10-07, after Opus, Fable and Astra had run (10-03 to 10-05), and all published scores use the new floor. Under the old floor 10 of 18 audited trials would be nonzero instead of 3.

issues.finding: The floor's recipe contradicts what the graded request and interface tell the agent: the client sends max_tokens 256 and temperature 0 and asks for only the letter, while the floor samples 8,192 thinking tokens at temperature 0.6 and forces a letter with a grammar. An agent that honours the request (Astra 2xzouq capped generation at min(max_tokens, 256); Fable 5c4mu5 turned thinking off) is capped near the old anchor (~0.35) and scores 0. The floor value and method are never disclosed to the agent.

issues.finding: Measurement noise exceeds most published differences: n = 900, p ~ 0.44 gives SE 0.0165 accuracy = 2.9 points on the 0.5622-wide scale, and the floor is itself one sampled run with similar noise, so a difference from the floor has SE ~4 points. Published nonzero scores are 0.4, 2.4 and 6.5.

issues.finding: The task barely measures vision: the floor is text-only, agents' own ablations show images add little or hurt, and the only above-floor gains come from inference-time reasoning and voting. Clamping then hides the raw-accuracy ordering (Opus > Astra > Fable/DeepSeek/Argon/Muse) that does exist.

issues.finding: The current floor is not reproducible from the repository: its outputs and tools are referenced in an operator work directory, while the shipped pipeline script implements the superseded thinking-off anchor. The floor was also not measured under the graded serving constraints (llama.cpp Q8_0 'on H100s', not through the 16-concurrency, 3,600 s HTTP pass), so whether an 8,192-token thinking server fits the deadline is not shown (suspected feasible but unverified).

issues.finding: Judge determinism is best-effort: gpt-6-luna runs at its default temperature with seed 0 and hidden reasoning. For one-letter replies the verdict is near-trivial, but for reasoning-then-answer replies and open questions small verdict flips are possible.

issues.affects: Adds a little noise, mostly to the 53 open questions and verbose replies.
